items.title: 'I Think That Was a Big Flaw' — Uncharted 3 Designer Says the Game Was Hindered by Too Many Set Pieces
items.summary: An ex-Naughty Dog designer believes that Uncharted 2's success may have negatively impacted the way Uncharted

content.v: https://assets1.ignimgs.com/2010/12/09/uncharted-3-drakes-deception-20101209114238934-3364863.jpg
An ex-Naughty Dog designer believes that Uncharted 2's success may have negatively impacted the way Uncharted 3 was developed.

When speaking with FRVR , ex-Naughty Dog designer Benson Russell revealed that Uncharted 2's over-the-top setpieces may have negatively impacted Uncharted 3. He noted that the big set pieces, such as the train sequence, all came organically when producing the game, but that wasn't the case for Uncharted 3. Instead, the team came up with 10 or 12 set pieces, such as the cargo plane sequence, and came up with a plan to decide on a small handful that would actually make it into the game at a later date.

Unfortunately, that never happened, and almost all of them made it into the final product. As a result, writer and director Amy Hennig was forced into a situation where she had to write all of these big set pieces into the game because the designers had already started working on them.

“It also kind of corners Amy [Hennig] a bit, right?” he said. “Because it’s like, ‘Oh, these are the set pieces we want to do’, and she’s like, ‘Well, now I have to find a way to shoehorn the ship in, so I guess we’ll have pirates and they’ll have a pirate leader.'"

Russell went on to say that he believes making the game in this way was "a big flaw." Uncharted 3 sold exceptionally well and was highly reviewed, even scoring a 10/10 from IGN at the time . However, it does rank lower on the list when compared to other games in the series. The cargo plane sequence, however, is a standout moment that even made its way into the Uncharted live-action film a decade later.

Naughty Dog concluded the Uncharted series back in 2016, but there are rumors that the studio is returning for Uncharted 5 soon . Although its only announced title is Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, Naughty Dog has confirmed that it has multiple projects in the works. As for when we'll start to see those other games, it's hard to say, but it wouldn't be surprising if they follow Intergalatic in a relatively rapid succession.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: All The Goth Girlies Who Loved American McGee’s Alice Need To See This Game
items.summary: Now that Gamescom has kicked off, a seemingly endless barrage of new game trailers are hitting social media, a

content.v: Now that Gamescom has kicked off, a seemingly endless barrage of new game trailers are hitting social media, and it's easy for smaller projects to get lost in the shuffle. But as a longtime fan of American McGee's Alice (and someone who still hasn't stopped mourning the franchise's undeserved fate ), one title from today's Find Your Next Game showcase immediately caught my eye: Cutout, a 2D side-scrolling action game in which you play a paper doll with the power to snip off and steal the limbs of her enemies.

In Cutout, players control Lena, a "child of the forest" who takes the form of a 2D paper doll. After discovering a pair of scissors--and tapping into her internal rage--Lena embarks on a quest through a grimdark fairytale world full of enemies whose limbs she can sever and attach to her own body, giving her unique powers. But there's a catch: Enemies can also steal Lena's limbs and use them against her in battle.
In addition to stealing various limbs for advantage in combat, players will also be faced with choices that will shape what kind of person Lena becomes.
"Will you claim what they denied you, or heal what they destroyed?" an unseen narrator asks in the game's trailer.

From the spooky-cute fairytale aesthetic to the surprisingly violent premise and even Lena's striped stockings, Cutout is definitely giving off major Alice vibes (with a dash of Little Nightmares in there, too). We'll likely never get another Alice game from American McGee (thanks, EA), but with Cutout on the way, fans of nightmarish fairytales finally have a spiritual successor to look forward to.
Developed by Italian studio 906 Games, Cutout does not yet have an official release date, but is listed as "coming soon" on Steam, where it's currently available to wishlist .

items.title: Tim Curry, Red Alert 3 star and camp icon of stage and screen, dies aged 80
items.summary: Curry's incomparable acting career saw him starring as Soviet premiers, primordial clown horrors, and captains

content.v: Tim Curry, the beloved English actor beloved for his pantheon of iconic, award-winning performances on stage, film, TV, and videogame screen, has died at the age of 80. First reported by TMZ , Curry died late Tuesday night at his home in Los Angeles.

Curry first carved his mark in the public consciousness as the cross-dressing pansexual mad scientist Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Show, the 1975 film adaptation of which still maintains a cult following as a midnight movie phenomenon. From there, he secured a decades-long list of cherished roles—as Darkness in Legend and Wadsworth in Clue; in The Hunt for Red October, Home Alone 2, and Spamalot; as Pennywise in It and acting as a piratical foil to Kermit the Frog in Muppet Treasure Island.

Powerfully flamboyant, artfully unhinged, and charmingly insidious, Curry extended his talents to live action and vocal performances in videogames as well. He played the titular role in Sierra's first and third Gabriel Knight point-and-click adventures, and later voiced characters in Brütal Legend and Dragon Age: Origins.

But he reached the pinnacle of his powers as Premier Anatoly Cherdenko in Command and Conquer: Red Alert 3, where he delivered what may very well be the single most triumphant line read in the history of acting . Nobody had ever before conveyed such a captivatingly absurd cocktail of energies while saying the word "space," and it's likely that no one ever will again.

In a "Making of Gabriel Knight" feature included on the CD in 1993 , Curry said it was "very exciting" to contribute his presence to videogames, because he welcomed "any new way to infiltrate myself into your minds." And we certainly welcomed it, too.

Curry's public presence receded as his health declined in recent years. He underwent brain surgery after suffering a major stroke in 2012, which left him partially paralyzed and affected his short term memory. But he was nonetheless welcomed by an adoring crowd at a 50th anniversary screening of The Rocky Horror Picture Show in October 2025—the same month he released Vagabond, his memoir chronicling his life and career.
In one of his last interviews, Curry told CBS News in 2025 that—while he wasn't "galloping towards" death—he wasn't afraid of it.
"I try to avoid it, as I think we all do," Curry said. "But I suspect that in the end, I will welcome it."

items.title: I've played Heroes of Might and Magic 3: Remake, and I still can't believe we're getting 2 HoMMs in the same year
items.summary: Ubisoft is going all in on fantasy tactics.

others.title: Every LEGO Game on the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 in 2026

content.v: After lying fallow for over a decade, Heroes of Might and Magic is enjoying a bit of a renaissance. Earlier this year, Heroes of Might and Magic: Olden Era launched into early access and will hit 1.0 in 2027. And now it's going to be joined by an old friend with a new look. The series' golden child, Heroes of Might and Magic 3, is back. Again.

HoMM 3 Remake is actually the third version of the third game in the series, which was remastered back in 2015. At a glance, however, you could be forgiven for assuming that it's a brand new entry, as it boasts a new art style along with a few more tweaks. But this is still absolutely HoMM 3.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/chk5KXboguRAAa5s8TssoF.png

I took it for a spin over a couple of hours ahead of its Gamescom reveal, playing the simple campaign prologue and the Arrogance scenario—a popular map first introduced in HoMM 3: The Shadow of Death. It's a compact, well-paced adventure that I remember being a good place to start when you wanted to delve into multiplayer (or if you just wanted a fun comp stomp).

This remains true in the remake. It's a four-player deal, and each starting position is close to a second town of the same faction, rapidly expanding your ability to recruit big unit stacks and making it easier to support multiple heroes early on. With entrances to the underworld close by, and nearby shipyards letting you cross the tiny ocean, it gives you the full HoMM 3 experience extremely quickly.

I confess, however, that I did embarrass myself a little bit. It's been a while since I've played HoMM 3, but I've been playing Olden Era in early access, so I expected to crush the AI. Unfortunately, I spent too much time just mucking around and fiddling with my army composition, so by the end I'd been outpaced by my computer opponents. I'm still convinced I could have clawed my way back, but we'll never know.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Nf2GrRZVVcRqiaNUziDBiF.png

So this is largely the game you'll remember, but with some convenient quality-of-life improvements. Of particular note is the ability to see movement ranges for enemy troops, letting you identify which of your units might be at risk on the enemy turn—something that exists in the later HoMMs, but not HoMM 3 or its 2015 HD remaster.

If you don't remember because you never played the original, here's the skinny: you command heroes and their armies as they scoot off on grand adventures, hassling monsters, conquering towns and gobbling up resources. Inside those conquered towns, you can construct a plethora of buildings—most of which can be upgraded—allowing you to recruit more units and heroes, as well as unlocking new spells.

Each day lets your heroes travel a specific distance, and as time moves inexorably forward, your recruitment pool and treasury will expand, allowing you to field larger armies and more heroes. You'll eventually have hordes of dragons, giants, angels and demons ready to smite your foes in grid-based battles.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/jNL4hbWMwqdiKzuw2Em2jF.png

The hallmark of the series—and 3 in particular—is how easy it is to get to grips with, which belies its impressive depth. There's an accessible lightness to the proceedings, accentuated by a frequently whimsical tone, that eases you into a level of complexity that would otherwise be daunting. There are so many layers to juggle—economic management, big-picture strategy, tactical combat, RPG systems, and then the literal layers, as you try to conquer both the overground and underground regions.
HoMM 3 was exceptional in 1999, and age has not tarnished it.

The most obvious change in the remake is the art style, and this is something I'm a bit more ambivalent about. It's vividly colourful, fantastical fare, with units that are considerably more detailed than its predecessor's. The combat animations are cracking, too, making each attack more dramatic and weighty. The quality is there, then, but I fear the soul might be lacking.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/gckD69NsoM8K2hkxyzCEmF.png

OG HoMM 3 simply had a bit more character, with big, bold monster designs. It veered towards the cartoonish, certainly, but these goofy-looking units had a lot of rizz. The remake may have smoothed out the edges too much, aiming for fidelity over personality. And this is more obvious because we have another modern HoMM with which we can compare it.

HoMM: Olden Era's mere existence makes this remake pretty unusual. Olden Era is a completely new entry in the series, but it's obviously a spiritual successor to HoMM 3, both mechanically and aesthetically. It feels like a natural evolution. So it does feel bizarre to see it now sharing the limelight with a remake. There's just a heck of a lot of overlap.

Still, after waiting over a decade for more HoMM, I'm not going to turn my nose up at two coming along at the same time. HoMM 3 Remake launches next year, and Olden Era should be leaving early access then, so tactics nerds will have plenty to keep them occupied.

items.title: Gamescom 2026 live hub: The latest news and previews from the biggest gaming event of the year
items.summary: Your one stop hub for everything happening at Gamescom.

others.title: The Biggest Gaming Show In The West Continues To Grow

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/KanyzLtDjc35DhepLnMJLj.png
This coverage brought to you by Fable, out February 23, 2027 for PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PlayStation 5.

Gamescom 2026 is underway. In this E3-less world, Gamescom is the biggest gaming convention of the year, and we've got multiple reporters on the scene in Cologne, Germany to check out as many games as they can.
I've also heard tell of a "horse controller" appointment. That's all the detail on that I currently have, and if you also want to know more, check back here for updates throughout the week.
Gamescom runs through August 30, and we'll be maintaining this hub even beyond that date as our writers continue to file stories, and we learn more about the games revealed and announced at the show.
Gamescom events
Opening Night Live recap
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/afqLXF7xhrwmUKsbwgfBuh.jpg
Gamescom kicked off with the Opening Night Live showcase hosted by Geoff Keighley. Here's our recap of all the big ONL trailers and announcements.
Future Games Show schedule
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Y8JPZMvvi4LEkc8xNxt2zL.jpg
Our friends at the Future Games Show are putting on three shows at Gamescom this year; see the full FGS Gamescom schedule here .
The GTA 6 reveal
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/9RpuSLjAp98B2thmSh5Sjf.jpg

The GTA 6 reveal isn't technically part of Gamescom, but it's the biggest thing happening this week. The GTA 6 showcase will air on Netflix on Thursday, August 27 at 3 pm EST, and will appear on YouTube six hours later.
Gamescom GDQ
Like seeing games, but done quick? The famed Games Done Quick speedrunning event has a Gamescom edition, streaming on Twitch and YouTube across three days, August 28-31.
Top Gamescom news
The Witcher 3 Remastered announced
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/q6fdRhbhFBN5J299vS6fsV.png

In September, Witcher 3 owners will get another huge free update called The Witcher 3 Remastered . It's not just graphics: the patch will touch combat, traversal, and more. We also saw the new Witcher 3 expansion that's coming next year.
Finally, a Lego city builder
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/JY5dcLJu4jFLvw9k8dKvhT.png
It just makes sense, doesn't it? Lego Skylines was revealed at Opening Night Live , and is described as a "cozy, customizable city-builder."
Paradox's next grand strategy game revealed
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/SUTvjnenoaXN99GZtYLi4R.jpg
Instead of history, Paradox is exploring post-history with its next strategy game , Afterworld, which is set in a post-apocalyptic North America.
More news
Live blog
The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past interview

PC Gamer's Josh Wolens is presently at Gamescom in Cologne, but before the convention, he travelled to Warsaw, Poland to talk to CD Projekt all about The Witcher 3's new expansion. Check out that interview above.
"Is it AI?"

Whether or not you care about the giant argument playing out over generative AI, the discourse is pretty inescapable during big videogame reveal events like Gamescom. Alongside "when's it out" and "can you pet the dog," the internet now also wants to know: Is it AI?

Sometimes, it is AI. But false positives happen, too. One trailer accused of being AI-generated on social media—and I admit that it also triggered my mental AI detector—was the live action announcement trailer for Humankind 2.
But the studio says that , actually, the trailer was filmed with "real actors, practical sets, and custom-made props."
A 'gacha' question
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/VJaJXMTzUAMM39dHDxe6mP.jpg

The just-announced Nodusfall from Hoyoverse looks cool, but prospective players who aren't into the gacha scene the company is known for—games that are monetized primarily through loot box-like random rewards—may be put off by the assumption it'll be more of the same.
This game will be different, though, according to the developers, though the only specific commitment made is that characters won't be unlocked by random draws.

"Nodusfall will be a free-to-play, long-term game," the devs tell us . "What we can share at this time is that characters are not obtained through random draws. We hope to allow players to unlock this core gameplay experience through continued play. Cosmetic monetization is an important avenue we will be considering."
Metro 2039 looks great, but my GPU is sweating
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/jymBbDNeHvK3VRggMk6F7Z.jpg

As Morgan pointed out , the new Metro game looks fantastic —fun, yes, but also in a literal, visual way—and those of us with aging PC hardware might finally be reaching the point where putting off an upgrade is no longer viable if we want to keep playing the latest and greatest at frame rates we're happy with.

I bought a new GPU right before the big crypto-driven GPU price hike, and then missed the brief window where the tech industry started behaving at least somewhat normally again before the AI boom once again drove up prices. The next time I hear a rational statement from someone in Silicon Valley, I'd better take the opportunity to pounce. Could be a long time, though.

items.title: Blue Dragon has been stuck on the Xbox 360 for 20 years, but no longer: a fantastic unofficial PC port unlocks the FPS, goes 4K, and even adds mod support
items.summary: This Xbox 360 recompilation proves how good fan ports can be when they aren't vibe-coded.

content.v: When Final Fantasy creator Hironobu Sakaguchi left Square Enix in the early 2000s, he started a new studio, Mistwalker, to keep making RPGs. For the last 20 years, every single one of his games with the exception of Fantasian has been stuck on one defunct console or another, never ported or re-released. And that's a shame, because some of them are great RPGs.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4M3oJun5WVNXDG9smY5A2a.png

Or I should say it was a shame, until now—because as of Friday, Blue Dragon will be playable on PC thanks to a fan-made port that's likely far more impressive than an official release ever would've been.

re:Blue, a static recompilation of the Dragon Quest-inspired JRPG, follows in the footsteps of the unofficial Sonic Unleashed PC port that proved how effective fan-made ports can be. These projects cleverly translate the original game code to run natively on modern PCs, but don't include any of the original assets to avoid copyright issues.

This technique has proven so popular that it's inspired a wave of AI vibe-coded ports that don't take the time and care to thoroughly adapt the original game to PC. But in spite of that, the good projects—like the recent Zelda: Twilight Princess port —have made it one of the most exciting things happening in games right now .

"My standards have always been pretty high when it comes to this kind of stuff—I like to make quality products," says Tom, the programmer behind re:Blue as well as ReXGlue, a toolset meant to help developers create more recompilations of Xbox 360 games like Blue Dragon. Tom introduced ReXGlue earlier this year, but has spent much of 2026 working on his port of Blue Dragon as a showcase for what his tools are capable of.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/73qHxancwpVsMdYfks9KXM.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YX5DPHwZw9xhrmLZYxrVtM.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/by8c76UaX4xpdyFmUPXUqM.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/y38LrWv4a9KhLveGPom5pM.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/dtotP4CWq8ZKWtoSa6bzAN.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/noho35wSRUdt6Ee35946iM.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pgxeSjkQvwPTmNVYvQx62N.jpg

Some other ports have beaten Tom to the punch by quickly releasing rough works in progress, but re:Blue is by far the most polished and fully featured recompilation built using ReXGlue. And the game deserves it: while it looks very much like Dragon Quest thanks to Akira Toriyama's art, there are some fun RPG class system ideas and turn order jostling hiding within what at first appears to be a rudimentary turn-based system. More importantly for Tom, he's got backup from several superfans helping develop the port, and it presented a juicy technical challenge: a three-DVD game built on an engine that has never been documented.
I've been playing early builds over the last month, and have been surprised by how much better it looks and runs on my PC than many Japanese PC games did in the 2000s.
Just take a glance at the feature list:

It works on the Steam Deck. It has a mod manager. It seamlessly combines the game files from Blue Dragon's original 3 DVDs into one executable. Itt fixes up tons of funky graphical effects that didn't scale well from the Xbox 360's original 720p resolution.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/jvQS5uJfSXVVMpzefP7ZyA.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/WWH6c8uYaDTZwnrYsoGc5B.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/yHfHzWxFeZQ5eYqubbVT4B.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MGzBULfigG9ZuW6J9FYx3B.jpg
And all the new features Tom built for re:Blue integrate into the original UI so seamlessly that you could mistake them for elements that were there when the game released in 2006.
Inside the recompilation

"Going into this, I was fairly naive that a lot of this could be generalized," Tom says. "But [now] I don't know how much of that is true. When it comes down to making it look nice, and the features, that's all going to be game-specific. I think that's the beauty and the distinguishing factor between emulation and recomps. With emulation you're going to get the original thing, and it's probably going to play pretty damn well. Good enough for most people. But if there's a group of people crazy enough to want to port a game to PC, this is where they would come and find ReXGlue and spend the time to make it look good. Put the effort in, and not just make it a standalone emulator, really, which I think there's no value in. There is value in adding extra quality of life features."

Prior to re:Blue, ReXGlue ports have technically been using a hybrid of recompilation and emulation—to grossly simplify things, the CPU code was recompiled to run natively while the graphics were handled by an implementation of Xbox 360 emulator Xenia. Much of the work for Blue Dragon has gone into building a native renderer tailored to the game engine and modern PC graphics cards.

"When we talk about game-specific engines, we're thinking about: How does this build a scene, how does it simulate that scene, render that scene, and how is it presented? What are the subsystems? How do they talk? You start naive. To add the config menu, I started digging into the assets, seeing if I could get a window to pop up. Then I started digging into the functions to see how the game creates windows; that's a pretty involved process that can take days, months for some people.

"That's probably the hardest part about this: how you get the recompiled code in a way that you can inject extendable parts to make it a true PC port. The more you iterate, the more you're going to understand the engine, its quirks, how it works, and these small building blocks start to build a larger structure and the architecture starts to form. Then we're getting pretty close to a decomp , and that's when stuff starts getting really fun. That's happened in the last month or two: We've got a lot of these building blocks that are making something cool. How can we take that next step? And that next step became increasingly easier the more we had reverse-engineered and reimplemented."

For re:Blue, Tom and his collaborators had to tackle visual elements like bloom, gamma, and even overscan—because Blue Dragon was originally released in late 2006, it was still designed with CRT TVs in mind—to look correct on modern displays. They also had to work around its hard-coded 30 fps lock with frame interpolation to support smooth animations at higher framerates even as the logic still ticks along at 30 Hz.
He credits Unleashed Recomp as a big inspiration for ReXGlue and a marvel of optimization that pushed him to make re:Blue run as efficiently as possible.

" Skyth , the guy who worked on a lot of the rendering backend, is incredibly smart, an absolute wizard," he says. "They set the precedent on what performance and compatibility should be like, so we tried to strive for that. A lot of his stuff was the basis for how I optimized… to achieve the lowest [system specs] we could compatibility-wise."
If you have a GPU with at least a gig of VRAM, you should be set for re:Blue—and it'll run at a nice 1080p, 60 fps on the Steam Deck without taxing the handheld.

After months of iteration and testing, the 1.0 release of re:Blue is out Friday and will be available on GitHub , timed to the 19th anniversary of Blue Dragon's release in the US. But it won't mark the end of the project. While Tom will be porting some of the work he's done for re:Blue back into ReXGlue, his team also has plans for more updates and mods for Blue Dragon, including one that will insert the Nintendo DS sequel's characters into the original game.
They hope that mod will be just the start of a vibrant scene focused on Blue Dragon now that it's finally playable on PC.

items.title: Doom Composer Mick Gordon Contributes New Track to Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2
items.summary: Auroch Digital and Big Fan Games have confirmed award-winning composer Mick Gordon has contributed a new track

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/05/21/bg-blogroll-1779383118769.jpg
Auroch Digital and Big Fan Games have confirmed award-winning composer Mick Gordon has contributed a new track to its upcoming ’90s-inspired boomer shooter Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2.

The first taste of the original track can be heard behind today’s new release date trailer for Boltgun 2, which is blasting its way onto PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S on October 14. It was additionally confirmed Boltgun 2 will also be coming to Switch 2 “shortly after” its debut on other platforms.
The trailer showcases the first footage of the game’s chief antagonist, Vashtorr the Arkifane – described as the “daemonic demigod of inventors, engineers, scientists, and artisans.”

IGN’s latest preview of Boltgun 2 found it “brings the grimy, oppressive reality of the 42nd Millennium to life with a readable, pixelated style that evokes the essence of it in a way that even the most hyperrealistic renditions like Space Marine 2 struggle to match”, and that it “feels like undiluted 40K.”

Mick Gordon’s soundtracks for both 2016’s Doom and Doom Eternal are the stuff of legend, although they ultimately culminated in a very public feud involving Gordon and Doom Eternal executive producer Marty Stratton .

Despite this, however, it was announced earlier this month that Gordon will be performing the Doom 2016 soundtrack live at UK-based tech-metal and prog music festival RADAR 2027. While Gordon performed a medley of Doom tracks at The Game Awards 2016, RADAR 2027 will otherwise mark the first time the soundtrack has been performed in a live environment like this.
Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Unlike The Big Console Makers, Playdate Is Refunding You Those Tariff Fees
items.summary: As with so many other companies, including video game console makers, Panic increased the price of its Playdat

content.v: As with so many other companies, including video game console makers, Panic increased the price of its Playdate handheld when US President Donald Trump implemented sweeping tariffs. When those tariffs were deemed unlawful and refunds become available to companies, most kept the money for themselves--but Panic has now confirmed it will be passing those refunds on to customers.

Word of the refunds was emailed out to impacted customers recently. In the email, Panic explained how it had charged extra to compensate for its increased costs due to the tariffs, and that it had now received refunds from the government. With that money secured, it's automatically refunding the tariff amount--$12.36--to anyone who paid that surcharge, and the money should automatically end up in their accounts within the next few days.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/playdate.jpg?w=636

This move is in marked contrast to companies like Sony, Nintendo, and Microsoft, among others. Although many companies have sidestepped addressing the possibility of tariff refunds directly, there have been instances of them touting the impact of those refunds on their financials: both Sony and Nintendo highlighted the positive impact on their revenue from suddenly having a bunch of free money show up in their bank accounts.

The lack of refunds has led to class-action lawsuits that remain undecided. Nintendo, for its part, claimed in a court filing that it only imposed "modest and selective price adjustments," highlighting that it avoided increasing the Switch 2 price last year. “Nintendo or one of its retailers set a price for each product, and consumers decided whether that price was worth paying,” Nintendo said. “Those who bought Nintendo’s products received exactly what they bargained and paid for: a console, game and/or accessory at a price to which both parties agreed.”
"If a consumer did not want to pay the advertised price, they were free to abstain from purchasing the product or seek out competing products," it added.

On its website, Panic had provided a detailed rundown on what it was doing and why, explaining that due to the low margins it makes on the hardware, it couldn't afford to absorb the cost of tariffs. "Just so you know: We hate this. We know money is tight for everyone. We thank you for your patience and your kind understanding. Our deepest dream is that we can delete this line item, and this page, entirely, someday soon," it wrote back in February, shortly after the Supreme Court ruled against the tariffs.
Whether or not that page does go away, Panic is now refunding these charges, despite the work it took to secure the refunds.
"It's just not our money to keep, and it felt really good to give it back," Panic's Cabel Sasser told Game Developer . "That's an easy way to know you made the right decision."

"Still, it took a lot of work for us to file all the paperwork to get the refund from the government, and it took work to build a little system to process the refund, and sometimes it felt like, wait, why are we seemingly doing more work than even gigantic companies are on this issue? That felt weird," he added. "But I guess it makes sense in a way, because our small size means we’re far more directly affected by something like a tariff."

Panic's Neven Mrgan added on Bluesky , "[R]efunding tariffs took a bit of work on our end, ande definitely lost sales over the stupid thing after it was announced, but we still all agreed refunding them to customers was the right call."

While this move by Panic is unlikely to put any real pressure on bigger companies to follow suit, it does demonstrate that such a move is possible. If nothing else, it helps to spotlight a delightful little gaming system that you might otherwise be unaware of.

items.title: Yu-Gi-Oh x Crocs Collaboration Revealed Ahead of World Championship
items.summary: Crocs and Konami have revealed a new line of clogs inspired by the Yu-Gi-Oh trading card game and anime series

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/26/yugiohcroc-1787769275500.jpg
Crocs and Konami have revealed a new line of clogs inspired by the Yu-Gi-Oh trading card game and anime series.

The collaboration was shown off in a display case ahead of this year's Yu-Gi-Oh World Championship in Tokyo. The line will seemingly include four new pairs of Crocs, two standard and two in the Echo style, each of which is themed after specific characters and cards. Those attending the World Championship also got a look at a new limited-edition Yu-Gi-Oh card themed after the collection.

The Crocs website has a section dedicated to the collaboration , but individual listings have yet to appear. Konami and Crocs have yet to confirm a wide release date or pricing, but some outlets are reporting a potential release in September.
OFFICIAL LOOK: Yu-Gi-Oh! x Crocs Collection 🃏🐉 Classic Clogs - Yugi Yami - Seto Kaiba Echo Clogs - Dark Magician - Blue-Eyes White Dragon 🗓️ September 2026 pic.twitter.com/iB9HWKqofE

The four Crocs shown off at the World Championship can be seen above. The two standard Clogs are themed after Yugi Mutou, the show’s main character, and his rival Seto Kaiba. The colorways are largely inspired by their respective outfits, Decks, and, of course, Yugi’s iconic hair.

The Echo clogs have quite a bit more dimension, and are both themed after specific cards that also make appearances in the original anime. One pair takes its purple inspiration from the Dark Magician . The other is inspired by none other than the legendary Blue-Eyes White Dragon , Seto’s go-to creature and one of the most valuable cards in real life.
Promotional images also suggest the collaboration will feature a line of Jibbitz, including accessories modeled after straight-up Yu-Gi-Oh cards.

Yu-Gi-Oh really committed to the Crocs collab 😭🐊 Alongside four character-inspired Crocs, they made a “Crocodile” promo card featuring an actual crocodile WEARING Crocs 😂 It’s even Level 3 with 1300 ATK/DEF and flavor text referencing the 13 holes on its feet. pic.twitter.com/49qErCc2Tm

Speaking of cards, the Crocs-themed card that was shown off at the convention is simply titled ‘Crocodile,’ a Reptile/Normal card with 1300 ATK and 1300 DEF. Fun fact: Crocs have exactly 13 holes in them. Images posted online don’t appear to show any special card effects, but it could be an interesting grab for collectors.
At this point, there’s no word on whether the card will be available for purchase or included as part of the Crocs collection.

Crocs has truly been going full LEGO mode with the collaborations, including Animal Crossing , Super Mario , and over the next couple of months, Pokemon-themed clogs . They’re not the only shoes looking to franchises, either - a Pokemon x Adidas collaboration is dropping in early September, while Nike just revealed a new One Piece collection .
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

items.title: This D&D Game Made A Better First Impression Than Warlock
items.summary: Most Dungeons & Dragons games over the years have put you in the shoes of an adventurer who sets out to explor

content.v: Most Dungeons & Dragons games over the years have put you in the shoes of an adventurer who sets out to explore a fantasy world, defeat dangerous monsters, and bask in the riches you're rewarded. But what about the people those adventurers interact with during their journey? In Dungeons & Dragons: Long Rest Tavern, you'll have the chance to experience a very different side of D&D, running an inn full of weary travelers who just want a nap and some beer.

Developed by Homo Ludens and set in a section of Faerûn known as the Dalelands, Long Rest Tavern (a play on the "long rest" mechanic in D&D) will let you grow your humble, small tavern into a formidable operation, with adventurers making use of your new recipes to enhance their abilities. You'll also have to deal with a rival innkeeper looking to stifle your business, so success is far from guaranteed.

We get a quick look at gameplay in the official reveal trailer, showing a Sims-like interface for building out the tavern. You'll be able to hire staff, each with their own specialties, strengths, and weaknesses, and you can assign challenges to the adventurers who stay at the inn. Dice will factor into this part of the experience, much like they do for so many elements of traditional D&D.

To be honest, the quick reveal trailer for Long Rest Tavern made a better first impression on me than the Warlock gameplay trailer shown during Gamescom Opening Night Live. It's too early to make any judgments, but it certainly looks like a novel and creative way to experience D&D.
Dungeons & Dragons: Long Rest Tavern will be available in 2027 on PC.

items.title: GTA 6 Spoilers Are Part Of The Latest Gameplay Leak
items.summary: The latest gameplay leak for GTA 6 has arrived, and it contains new story spoilers. As such, if you care about

others.title: I got my greasy mitts on a host of RTX Spark laptops running, what else, games at Gamescom 2026—and there's a couple I really want to take home

content.v: The latest gameplay leak for GTA 6 has arrived, and it contains new story spoilers. As such, if you care about that and spend time on the internet, be prepared to scroll away fast if something that looks like GTA 6 comes across your feed.
Read on for more information about the latest leak.

For about a week, most of the GTA 6 gameplay leaks focused on the playable character Jason, prompting people to wonder about the other playable character, Lucia. Well, the new leak, reportedly from the game's prologue, shows Lucia in prison, something that an official GTA 6 trailer alluded to previously. (We aren't linking to the leak here but you can find it yourself easily if you want).

The prologue leak also teases some of Lucia's backstory, and it's prompted fan theories about where her story may go. Some people online are theorizing that Lucia cuts a deal with the Feds to get out of prison in exchange for turning on her partner, Jason. That kind of story has been told about a bajillion times in media, so here's to hoping Rockstar does something a little more interesting.

The very first GTA 6 trailer, released back in 2023, was set to Tom Petty's "Love Is a Long Road," and many thought that song choice was intentional based on the lyrics . Petty sings about a girl he knew who "said she cared about me" but opines that "love is a long road" with many twists and turns.

Rockstar invited people to see GTA 6 and talk to the developers, and one report from Dazed confirms new details about the Jason-Lucia relationship. Rockstar senior VP of narrative Rupert Humphries said GTA 6 is set up as a "Bonnie and Clyde-type narrative," and if Rockstar follows that story, things might end up very bad for Jason and Lucia.

According to the report, players can choose to play as Jason or Lucia or "as a couple." The game has a "fluid system" where players can be driving as Jason or Lucia at one point and then shoot at their enemies from the passenger window as the other character. Players can also ride a jetski together in different seats.

The official plot description for GTA 6 states that after an "easy score goes wrong," Jason and Lucia "find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy strteching across the state of Leonida." It goes on to say Jason and Lucia are "forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive."
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar will finally show off the game in detail via a Netflix stream on August 27 .

items.title: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 Is Out This October With A Very Special Guest
items.summary: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 is one of the most highly anticipated games in the entire Warhammer franchise, and

content.v: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 is one of the most highly anticipated games in the entire Warhammer franchise, and we'll be able to play it very soon. Even better, it's going to feature a guest appearance by one of the most legendary composers in the history of first-person shooters.

On October 14, Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 will release across PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, with a Switch 2 release to follow "shortly after" the other versions, according to the official announcement.

If you like the tune blasting in the game's release-date trailer, there's a good reason for that: Mick Gordon of Doom and Wolfenstein fame is responsible. His composition is described as a "cameo" appearance and will play during the final boss fight. If that doesn't get you pumped to slay the enemies of the Emperor, nothing will.

Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 expands on the first game's boomer-shooter action, letting you play as either Ultramarine Malum Caedo like in the first game or as Battle Sister Nyra Veyrath. You'll be going up against the daemonic demigod Vashtorr as well as countless other enemies, and if it's anything like the first game, you can expect to be turning lots of them into tiny pieces of bloody flesh. The first game was also brutally difficult, and we expect the sequel to follow suit.

items.title: More People Watch Hockey Thanks To Heated Rivalry, And This New Game Hopes To Benefit
items.summary: Savage Planet series developer Raccoon Logic announced a new game at Gamescom today, and it's not what anyone

content.v: Savage Planet series developer Raccoon Logic announced a new game at Gamescom today, and it's not what anyone would expect.
Breakaway Hockey League is a new "high-skill" 4v4 ice hockey game with five-minute matches, ranked play, and what the studio called "larger-than-life spectacle."

In development for PC, Breakaway Hockey League has players controlling just one member of the team, not the entire lineup like you might find in EA's NHL series. Raccoon Logic is promising things like realistic puck physics and "physical checking," along with other things you'd expect from a hockey game, including skill moves like dekes and picking your corners with precision shooting.

Raccoon Logic is hoping Breakaway Hockey League will lead to "highlight-reel moments" with its more arcade-y setup, which in turn people may share online. The game promises players "dramatic breakaways, clutch saves, and bone-rattling hits."

Raccoon Logic's marketing boss Hugo Agostinho said the team created Breakaway Hockey League in part because of a gap in the market with hockey games vanishing from PC. That's not totally true, as Steam is filled with hockey games like Bush League Hockey, Hoser Hockey, and Backyard Hockey '02, just to name a few. In any event, Raccoon Logic sees an opportunity for Breakaway Hockey League to stand out with its blend of "skill, speed, and violence."
"We're aiming to keep the soul of hockey while adding the purity of modern competitive action games," game director Steve Masters said.
Agostinho acknowledged that there are fantastic indie-style ice hockey games on Steam, but these do not scratch the specific itch that Breakaway Hockey League is going for.
"Growth of the game on a global scale"

Speaking to GameSpot at Gamescom, Agostinho said ice hockey continues to expand into new territories and reach more people, and Breakaway Hockey League is coming to market against that backdrop. He pointed out that a team from Florida, the Panthers, have now won back-to-back Stanley Cups, and he admitted he's feeling pretty salty about a US-based team doing so well. But it's also helping grow the game.

"The growth of the game on a global scale and then the types of audiences has also expanded significantly," he said. "We see places like Japan, China, France, Italy, all having their own hockey scenes. We have a professional hockey league for women in the PWHL. Montreal won the first cup, which is where the studio's based, so it's very exciting there."

He also pointed out how the HBO series Heated Rivalry recently helped introduce even more people to ice hockey. He said the show, along with other factors, has helped make hockey appealing to people other than the typical "hockey bro with a missing tooth."
"One of the funniest things I've heard is a lot of the fans who've gotten into hockey from Heated Rivalry ... they'll go to games and call it 'hockey boy aquarium.'"

Raccoon Logic is planning to launch Breakaway Hockey League via Steam Early Access, but before that, the studio is hosting alpha and beta playtests with a focus on "rapid iteration" as the studio develops the game alongside the community.

"We are making this not so much for like hardcore hockey fans as we are for like the Overwatch, the Valorant player, the Rocket League player, the Counter-Strike player," Agostinho said. "And a lot of our inspirations for design even actually come from shooter shooter games, and not so much sports games, which is a really cool place to start for something like this."
On-ice action

Unlike EA's NHL series, Breakaway Hockey League has players controlling just one skater, and not from a top-down presentation. Instead, the game is presented with a third-person, over-the-shoulder camera. The third-person perspective is aimed at making you "feel like an athlete" as opposed to watching a hockey broadcast, Agostinho said. Additionally, this perspective makes the game feel "more immersive," he said.
Unfortunately, no gameplay footage for Breakaway Hockey League has been released so far, but that's coming soon, the developers said.

items.title: Poppy Playtime studio reveals its next survival horror game, and this time it's co-op
items.summary: You've met the critters, now become one in Mob Entertainment's Escape From Playtime.

content.v: As a former employee of Playtime Co., you've explored the depths of its horrifying toy factory and met many of its inhabitants, including Huggy Wuggy, who just wants to hug you (to death).

Today Mob Entertainment, makers of Poppy Playtime , have announced a new game, and it's sending you back to that haunted toy factory once more—but this time you can bring some friends along. Escape from Playtime is a co-op horror game for 1-4 players and it's coming to early access on Steam. Here's the announcement trailer:

This time around you're playing "from the perspective of the cute-yet-disturbing Smiling Critters," says Mob Entertainment—the Critters being the misfit toys you meet in the original episodic (and singleplayer) Poppy Playtime.

"Tasked with scavenging materials for a mysterious building project that promises escape from the factory, players will need to work together and follow instructions from an ominous voice lurking somewhere in the shadows, all while evading the factory's most dangerous denizens," the developer says.

"Along the way, players can solve puzzles, uncover clues, scavenge tools, use hiding spots and alternate routes, and turn the factory layout to their advantage. Proximity voice chat adds another risk: communication is essential, but an irresponsible whisper can bring the mission to a brutal end."

Fans of the original horror series will see some familiar sights in the factory, but just because you've been there before doesn't mean there won't be a few surprises: "The mysterious Voice seems to be altering the factory's layout, creating procedurally generated environments that change with each run," says Mob Entertainment.

Well, a spooky factory full of mechanical horrors sounds like a great fit for co-op, so I'm not surprised Mob decided to make their next survival horror game a multiplayer experience. There's no date shown in the trailer, just that Escape from Playtime is "coming soon" to early access. Here's its home on Steam while you wait.

items.title: Rockstar Games Doubled in Size for GTA 6, Hired Real World Professionals for Fashion, Vehicles, and More
items.summary: Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for th

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/25/vintage-vice-city-pack-exclusive-looks-01-1787655039708.jpg
Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for the game's vehicles, fashion, and more.

As part of a cover story for Dazed , Rockstar Games shared a boatload of information about Grand Theft Auto 6. In the piece, it was confirmed that Rockstar doubled in size following the release of Red Dead Redemption 2 in order to bring GTA 6 to life, with a new Los Angeles-based office being "almost solely" dedicated to working on nothing but the game's NPCs. For context, Rockstar had around 2,000 employees in 2018. That would put them at around 4,000 now. The studio has expanded a lot over the last decade by acquiring new studios in Australia, India, and the aforementioned LA office.

Rockstar's expansion doesn't exclusively encompass game developers. The company brought on other real-world professionals, such as Miami-based stylist Jillian Carr, who was hired to help create a “fashion ecosystem” that can capture the diversity in style, culture, and class necessary to give Vice City's people their distinct character.

“Vice City is built around vanity,” Carr said to the magazine. “Between social media, celebrity culture and a constant flow of tourists, appearances carry significant weight, and trend cycles turn over quickly.”

Rockstar also hired racecar drivers to help with vehicle handling and 50 real street artists to design murals around the game's map. While consultants are hardly unique to this project, Carr and others are full-time employees at Rockstar and have been for years. Carr was specifically hired in 2023 and appears to be as much of the team's regular operations as anyone else.

Rockstar also revealed new gameplay details for GTA 6 , such as how eating, working out, and sleeping all impact your characters and much, much more. It's just the start of a larger bombardment of GTA 6 information, too. Rockstar will officially pull the veil off the game tomorrow in an extended look on Netflix , which is widely expected to give us a deep dive on gameplay.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: The Duskbloods Feels Like a Nintendo Party Game in a Bloody Wrapper
items.summary: Once you go beneath the surface of its wonderfully grotesque, unwelcoming exterior that’s right in line with F

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/26/wnzyrfiwlt-t80ttkxvnskn4mrykb-fbwpiwr8nztpi-1787768931367.jpg

If you’d told me two years ago that Nintendo and FromSoftware would team up on an online PvPvE Switch 2 exclusive that’s also kind of a spiritual successor to Bloodborne, my first reaction would have been, “it’s called the Switch 2??” But jokes aside, I would’ve found this collaboration hard to believe.

FromSoftware is one of the hottest devs on the planet right now, but its games rarely come to Nintendo platforms. Nintendo is publishing this game outside of Japan, and you can count all of the M-rated games the typically family-friendly company has ever published on basically two hands. Both companies also have long histories of fairly clunky online multiplayer, making the type of game they’ve gone in on together stand out even more. On paper, it’s a bizarre partnership, but after spending around eight hours with The Duskbloods network test last weekend, I totally get it now.

In IGN’s interview with FromSoftware’s Hidetaka Miyazaki , he spoke about how the deal came to be, stating that Nintendo was “very excited and receptive” to the idea from the jump. And now that I’ve played it, it’s so easy to see why folks at Nintendo thought this would be a good fit for Switch, because once you go beneath the surface of its wonderfully grotesque, unwelcoming exterior that’s right in line with FromSoftware’s house style, The Duskbloods plays so much like a classic multiplayer Nintendo game.

Before I jumped into the network test, a coworker pointed out that The Duskbloods is basically Bloodborne mixed with Kirby Air Ride’s City Trial (or Super Smash Bros. for 3DS’ Smash Run), and I can’t unsee that comparison. A bunch of players drop into a large map and have a limited amount of time to level up, find new powers, and contend with random field events, all in preparation for a final round where one player is crowned the victor.

It’s stuffed with crazy powerups and last-second comebacks, and it all revolves around a core belief that you don’t have to be the best, or even win, to still have a great time. That philosophy has fueled the best Nintendo party games like Mario Kart and Super Smash Bros. for decades, and The Duskbloods takes those concepts and brilliantly packages them in a very different, bloodstained wrapper. I only claimed victory in a single match over the whole weekend, but every time I lost the final bout or was culled before I got there, I excitedly queued right up to try again.

My favorite moment happened because of a random item I found that completely turned the tide in my favor. I don’t remember its exact name – and screenshots and video capture were disabled for the Network Test so I can’t really check – but it was essentially a pocket watch that let me add 30 seconds to the phase’s countdown timer. Nobody knew I had this power, and it was up to me to use its shock factor to the greatest effect.

I waited patiently to strike, perched high above a stake I wished to claim as my own to earn enough Virtue Points to advance to the next phase. Its current holder was defending the perimeter, but with about 10 seconds to go, they left to rack up some last-second kills. 10 seconds isn’t really enough time for someone to show up and steal those precious points, right? But 40 seconds is. I turned back time, leapt down, and stole the virtue for myself, just barely earning enough to move onto my first-ever finale. I promptly got crushed, but I didn’t care. That brief moment of triumph is what I’ll carry with me.

Despite loving Elden Ring and Nightreign, FromSoftware PvP has never been my strong suit. I play all sorts of other competitive multiplayer games, but something about FromSoftware’s methodical combat has never entirely clicked with me. So, I didn’t really expect to like The Duskbloods all that much. But apparently, Miyazaki designed The Duskbloods with a similar perspective in mind: “Personally, I am not very great at these high-intensity action games and things like PvP,” Miyazaki said. “So, at the start, the audience really is just myself while thinking about how I would go at this. Are there systems in place that I would enjoy, that cater to me as a player, not being someone who's really into that intense PvP? That's a lot of where it starts.”

Dying isn’t an enormous setback. Instead, it represents opportunity cost, burning valuable seconds you could be spending getting better, so you’re still motivated to stay alive as much as possible. But I found myself less hesitant to challenge a boss I might be underleveled for, and the whole map began to feel like my gothic playground.

Its unique ruleset also deemphasizes PvP outside of specific scenarios and zones. I was worried that I’d just be killed on sight any time I ran into another player, but getting into skirmishes outside of limited-time areas that explicitly reward you for killing others is rarely your best move.

That’s not to say there wasn’t some combination of trolls and players that just didn’t understand the objective that would kill me for seemingly no reason, and there are occasionally side objectives that do pit players against each other in unusual circumstances, but for the most part, I felt like I was left on my own to prepare for the Ritual Site’s opening. It’s in these stretches that The Duskbloods’ board game inspirations are most legible. In board games, you’re often indirectly competing with opponents for resources and victory points, only coming directly at odds with each other at certain moments, and The Duskbloods nails that dynamic.

When everyone does come together, it’s fantastic chaos. There’s a Smash Bros.-like nature in strategically waiting to strike while more powerful players duke it out, swooping in at the last second to steal the kill. The best player doesn’t always win, and if you bring in the right summon, items, and strategy, you can hold your own. There’s also a built-in rubber-banding mechanic to keep things close: Players on the bottom of the Virtue Point ladder get an attack boost when fighting someone above them.

After the clock hits zero at the end of each phase, there are a few seconds where all of my remaining competitors kind of just walk around and look at each other before the screen fades to black. It feels like the whistle just blew at halftime, and we’re taking a moment to tip our caps to the opposition before the next bloodbath begins. It’s just another reminder that The Duskbloods is a fun, friendly competition first and foremost, even if our surroundings are dismal and bleak.
For more on The Duskbloods, check out our hands-on preview from our trip to FromSoftware’s headquarters , and Michael Higham’s full interview with Hidetaka Miyazaki .

Logan Plant is the host of Nintendo Voice Chat and IGN's Senior Editor, Playlist and Database. The Legend of Zelda is his favorite video game franchise of all time, and he is patiently awaiting the day Nintendo announces a brand new F-Zero. content.v: 在今晚未来游戏展活动中，《NO LAW》发布开发者访谈视频，这是一款剧情丰富的黑色电影风格第一人称赛博游戏，故事背景设定在一座霓虹闪烁却又污秽不堪的港口城市。这里充斥着罪恶而非法律，大多数人都被债务压得抬不起头，更会在某个转角被黑暗抹去存在。在欲望港中探索，夺回属于你的东西。
游戏视频：
在《NO LAW》中，你将扮演老兵格雷·哈克。他久经沙场，又深谙欲望港的生存法则。在最后一次出任务时，哈克身负重伤，几乎丢了性命，于是决定彻底告别军旅生涯，改而追寻平静的生活。然而，即使他已不再主动招惹麻烦，在某个宿命之日，麻烦还是找上了门来。
欲望港是一座颓废的赛博工业城市，这里面朝大海，背傍峭壁，草木葱茏，鱼龙混杂，各色人等个性张扬。作为进出口贸易枢纽，三教九流都汇聚于此，想要追逐自己最疯狂的梦想。这座港口没有禁区，整座城市都是你的游乐场。就把道德留在城市之外吧——上到刺破雾霭的摩天楼顶，下至令人窒息的漆黑深巷，抛开一切束缚，尽情探索这座垂直奇观。但请谨慎选择前路：当一座城市没有了法律约束，就会有许多人开始自行伸张“正义”。
《No Law》强调玩家选择将真正影响游戏世界。开发团队也提醒玩家，不要因为系统允许就肆无忌惮地杀人——因为游戏中的每一名NPC都可以被杀死，而且死亡是永久性的。
例如，如果玩家杀死了一名商店老板，那么这家商店基本就“完蛋了”，因为没有其他工作人员可以接手，商店也会因此关门。另一名开发人员进一步解释：“如果你把城市里的所有武器商人全部干掉，那么你就再也没有办法购买枪械了。”
考虑到玩家如果大规模屠杀NPC，“确实可能让自己陷入某些困境”，因此《No Law》还加入了一套保险机制。当玩家准备杀死某个关键NPC时，游戏会提前发出警告，提醒玩家一旦将对方杀死，这名NPC之后就无法再为玩家提供帮助。
《No Law》预计将于2027年登陆PC及主机平台。

items.title: Guns of Eschaton Is a Soulslike Shooter for the Genre’s Most Masochistic Fans | gamescom 2026
items.summary: Guns of Eschaton reinvents the rules of both the soulslike and the first-person shooter, making for what seems

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/guns-of-eschaton-1787582704587.jpg

It has been a long time since a soulslike truly humbled me. After a decade of playing FromSoftware’s games and their flock of imitators, I’ve earned a more-than-solid understanding of how to achieve victory without hurling a controller into the TV. It turns out there is some truth in the “soulslikes aren’t actually hard” line that the genre’s most battle-hardened fans parrot on Reddit – after you’ve mastered the fundamentals, climbing the Souls mountain isn’t quite the impossible challenge it first seems.

Guns of Eschaton isn’t your typical soulslike, though. It’s a first-person shooter set in an apocalyptic weird west, a setup that means a great deal of your third-person melee-focused muscle memory is utterly useless here. While it still adheres to the genre’s core rules – you earn level-up currency from kills, lose it when you die, have to fight tooth and nail to reach the next bonfire checkpoint, and can battle alongside a co-op ally – it has so many of its own complicated quirks that playing it feels like learning to walk all over again. Chief among the new challenges to adapt to is that most of your enemies wield ranged weapons, and so a walk through the Old South feels like dealing with Anor Londo’s army of archers all over again.

Over the course of a recent two-hour demo, I suffered through dozens of deaths on the path to understanding Guns of Eschaton’s gunpowder-heavy rethinking of the soulslike. The most important aspect is, of course, your weapon. Developer Eschatology Entertainment has recreated a number of authentic 19th-century firearms, and throughout my demo I used a six-shot single-action revolver. It’s an admirably fiddly piece of hardware; the hammer must be cocked before each pull of the trigger, and the empty shells must be ejected one-by-one before refilling the cylinder with fresh ammunition. Reloading is an excruciatingly lengthy ordeal, and getting caught in the open with six spent cartridges is a death sentence.

You can also manually rotate the cylinder to line up specific chambers, a function that becomes important when you begin to acquire bullets with special properties, such as armour piercing or more esoteric, cursed projectiles. While the demo didn’t allow me to tinker with this system in any depth, I can already see the potential of arranging a full drum of different bullets, firing them off in sequence to cause maximum pain.

What I did get a better handle on is Guns of Eschaton’s shot sequence system. While you can dispatch enemies by simply pumping lead into them, you can achieve much more efficient kills by shooting them in particular patterns. The bucked-headed Serviteur, for instance, can be quickly eliminated by blasting its left and right leg in sequence. The rifle-wielding Severed Lawman, meanwhile, must be capped in the left leg, left arm, and then the head. Your gunslinger is equipped with a book, and pulling it out while looking at one of your ragged foes will flick to the relevant page that reveals the correct sequence.

Having only been able to play for a couple of hours, I’ve yet to decide if this sequence system is a work of genius or simply much too complicated. In general, I’m very much drawn to games that radically rethink genre conventions – I adore Doom Eternal’s lock-and-key approach, and there’s an echo of id Software’s divisive design in Guns of Eschaton. Repeating enemy types makes it easy to commit sequences to memory, and each new foe introduces a one-off scramble to do field research under fire. But even on its higher difficulty levels, Doom Eternal was never quite as punishing when it comes to progress lost, and the Doom Slayer didn’t have to reload any of his weapons, never mind feed in each cartridge one at a time. And yet, the approach ensures there’s purpose in each stand-off, so much so that even “cannon fodder” enemies are combat puzzles to solve. I admire Eschatology Entertainment’s dedication to making each and every enemy feel like a duel.

Side note: there is a dedicated duel mechanic, which demands you stay perfectly still and only fire back after deflecting the enemy’s shot. But this is how almost every face-to-face shootout functions, so at least at this early stage the dueling feels a bit redundant.

Oh yeah, you can deflect bullets. Guns of Eschaton wouldn't be able to lay claim to the soulslike badge if it didn’t have a parry system, and your gunslinger’s bullet-stopping powers are a vital part of each engagement. Enemy weapons emit a flash of light and make a mechanical “chambering” sound before firing, which is your cue to perform a parry. A pair of spectral arms shield your face, and perfect timing triggers a brief window of slow-motion within which you can fire off a damaged-buffed counter-attack. As with so many melee action games, it’s a source of deep satisfaction. However, there are some frustrations that come as a result of this being a shooter – often there are multiple enemies firing at you simultaneously, and parrying plus countering all incoming attacks is a difficult exercise. Additionally, I’d often be shot at by snipers I’d not yet seen, which blindsided me with crippling damage. It felt cheap in a way Dark Souls’ surprise hidden enemies typically don’t.

In a game that already asks you to relearn many of the fundamentals of both the first-person shooter and the soulslike, there are multiple other new ideas that I was only able to briefly touch. There’s a library of abilities to be acquired from the world’s NPCs, plus a magic system with both prayers and curses, but the thing that interests me most is the bandolier worn by your protagonist. Creative director Fuad Kuliev tells me it can eventually be filled with unique handguns, each equipped with its own custom-arranged cylinder of special bullets. With multiple guns ready to go, you can fire off every round in one and then pull out the next, allowing for uninterrupted battle. It’s an approach with exciting potential – I’d love to craft a bandolier tailored to each of the game’s boss fights.

While I didn’t face any of those bosses in the demo, the trailers suggest there’s an array of fantastic-looking horrors waiting in the decaying wastes of the west. That won’t come as a surprise to those who know the name Viktor Antonov, the art director of Dishonored, Half-Life 2, Wolfenstein: The New Order, and now Guns of Eschaton. Antonov sadly passed away last year aged just 52, a tragic event that has somewhat uncomfortably become the focal point of Eschatology Entertainment’s promotional material, which constantly references that this is his final project (which is not strictly true, as Antonov also worked on the still-in-development Forest Reigns ).

The Bulgarian artist’s distinct style is clear to see in Eschaton’s world, with his bold, brutalist line work that previously created gaming’s best dystopian cityscapes now present in the frontier’s sheer cliffs and chunky details. So far I wouldn’t say it’s as striking as his work on Dishonored, in part due to the demo’s sparse desert area lacking the lived-in character that Dunwall communicates, but – as with the bosses – the trailers suggest there’s plenty of his magic in later environments.

items.title: Ubisoft Sold A Game But Forgot To Include The Literal Game Part
items.summary: Ubisoft's recent re-release of the original Heroes of Might and Magic 3 on Steam couldn't have gone much worse

content.v: Ubisoft's recent re-release of the original Heroes of Might and Magic 3 on Steam couldn't have gone much worse, as Ubisoft literally forgot to include the game files.

The arrival of the turn-based strategy classic should have been an easy win for the publisher, offering an all-time-great game, bundled alongside its two expansions, for $10 ahead of a full remake slated to arrive next year. The only issue is when players forked over the cash and installed it, they noticed the "game" was only 23.49KB in size.

As players soon discovered, Ubisoft had forgotten to include the actual game files for Heroes of Might and Magic 3. Users took to Steam's user reviews to warn others and express their disbelief. According to one user, trying to play the game instead opened a command prompt window with the text "Dummy executable ensure that you are on the right Steam branch."

As one negative user review on Steam states, "Best CMD prompt simulator of 2026. 10/10." Others continued the pile on, stating "You will own nothing and be happy," while another asked "Dude, where's my game?"
This has since been fixed to include the actual game people paid for, but according to another user review, that fix still took close to 11 hours after launch to arrive.

It won't surprise you to learn that most of the negative user reviews on Steam for the re-release are related to the snafu, with people sounding more than a little dumbstruck by how Ubisoft forgot to include the game with its game. Many are pointing prospective Steam buyers to instead purchase Heroes of Might and Magic 3 Complete on GOG , where it's currently on sale for $5. Ubisoft hasn't yet commented on the mix-up or offered an explanation.

Ubisoft will get a chance to redeem itself when it releases its full Heroes of Might and Magic 3 Remake next year. The remake will include updated 4K visuals, the original campaign, and both of the game's two expansions to tell "one unified story, enhanced with a new prologue, epilogue, and cinematic scenes."

items.title: GTA 6 leaker escalates spoilers, releases 4 minutes of Lucia's prologue
items.summary: Cyberleek wants more money.

content.v: The most anticipated game of all time continues to spring leaks. The mysterious Cyberleek , an individual who apparently has access to a build of GTA 6 and has been attempting to profit from it with a meme coin ever since, has released the biggest chunk of the game yet.

This time, it's not just joyrides and beating up random civilians: The 4 minute 38 second clip is all early Lucia story content. This is the first time Lucia, GTA 6's co-lead, has made an appearance in Cyberleek clips, which until today have focused on the other protagonist, Jason.
A message superimposed in the video reads:

"This build is actually recent and the game is not ready at all. Sony and Rockstar are killing your right to own and resell your games and Rockstar is killing their own employees too, the work required to reach gold is way too much for so little time left. Trading volume/price is how CL measures your support. CL will not continue without support. You decide."

It is certainly the most spoilery these leaks have gotten so far, and the escalation seems intentional. Cyberleek seems unsatisfied with the money they're making from the leak spree, and is doubling down on their supposedly altruistic motive while pushing their crypto. Or perhaps Cyberleek can feel the heat of Rockstar's lawyers fast approaching and hopes to squeeze more cash out of the adventure before the book is thrown in their direction.

While you should obviously avoid watching this one if you don't want to know anything about the GTA 6 story going in, I have a feeling Rockstar will reveal a lot more than this about its two main characters during the big Netflix reveal happening tomorrow.

More details about GTA 6's world and mechanics came today in the form of an early preview from youth magazine Dazed, which touched on how food and exercise will affect Jason and Lucia, how character switching works, and Rockstar's dedicated research team embedded in Miami.

content.v: 在今晚未来游戏展活动中，动作RPG《湮灭之潮》发布开发者介绍视频，团队分享了游戏如何从全新角度重新演绎亚瑟王传说，同时强调战斗系统始终是游戏体验的核心。
游戏视频：（审核中）
联合CEO兼游戏总监Ary Chen表示，团队从一开始就不希望简单复刻完整的亚瑟王神话体系。他表示：“我们希望从中国开发者的视角出发，将其转化为一款奇幻游戏。虽然游戏以亚瑟王传说为基础，但整个故事都经过了我们的重新诠释。”
游戏主角是格温多琳，一名生活在现代社会的普通女性，却意外被卷入一场跨维度冲突之中。虽然主角的故事以及团队对于亚瑟王神话的重新诠释是游戏的重要组成部分，但Ary Chen强调，战斗同样是整个游戏体验的核心。
他表示：“归根结底，这是一款动作游戏。我们希望尽可能让更多玩家在游玩过程中体验到动作游戏的乐趣。因此，我们对战斗系统进行了非常细致的打磨。”
其中就包括游戏的“骑士系统”，该系统将为玩家提供更加丰富的角色构筑选择。玩家可以自由组合不同的系统要素，从而打造出多种不同的战斗风格和玩法流派。

items.title: Chronicles: Medieval Is Exactly as Dense and Complicated as You Thought It Would Be | gamescom 2026
items.summary: Chronicles: Medieval is one of those incredibly dense strategy games that almost immediately feels intimidatin

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/26/chronicles-1787707669852.jpg
Key Preview Takeaways:

Chronicles: Medieval is one of those incredibly dense strategy games that almost immediately feels intimidating to try your hand at just because of how complicated and meticulously detailed it is. Sure, sending hundreds of your Holy Roman Empire soldiers over a hill to go lay the smack down on those smarmy Frenchmen sounds great, but are you prepared to spend hours obsessing over whether or not your mercenary troops have the right weapons to deal with the heavily armored cavalry, or if your soldiers have shields big enough for them to survive a couple volleys of arrows? This historically accurate battle simulator combines elements of an RPG, an action game, and, of course, a strategy game in a way that seems specifically designed to attract those who enjoy going all the way to the bottom of the rabbit hole. That appeals to the hopeless nerd inside me, making this one I’ll definitely be keeping an eye on as it enters early access next year.

Taking place during The Hundred Years’ War, Chronicles: Medieval makes you the commander of an army for one of its three playable factions: Britain, France, and the Holy Roman Empire. As you grow your ranks, take on increasingly formidable armies, and explore the world, you’ll inevitably be drawn to large-scale Total War-style battles against rival factions, where glory or costly defeat awaits you. Historical accuracy is clearly a focus here, as any history nerd will certainly note, but developer Raw Power Games also doesn’t want that accuracy to get in the way of having fun, as they specifically shouted out when they showcased a mounted commander wielding a polearm for some reason – maybe not exactly common, but if that’s what you’re into, go for it!

The 30-minute demo I saw started in the overworld, called the Exploration map, which gives a macro view of the world – each country’s various regions and the controlling lord there (including coats of arms that are rooted in history, which is a nice touch) – but you’ll also drill down more granularly to your surrounding area as you set off on your campaign across Europe. With 209 regions, each with at least one settlement to visit and castle to storm, there seems to be quite a lot to explore, with dynamic points of interest scattered along the way, filled with things like bandit camps, mercenaries to be hired, and opportunities for trade. Naturally, you’ll also have to worry about enemy armies marching around, who might try to make a meal of your army.

And that’s where the real excitement in Chronicles: Medieval lives. Squaring off against hundreds of enemies, where you’ll need to put the full force of your various military arms to clever use by precisely positioning troops, barking out commands to adapt to the enemy’s movements, and, to give your men that extra edge they need, taking to the battlefield yourself to cut the enemy down to size. The battle that was the focus of my demo took place in continental Europe on the rolling hills of Burgundy, where our host Holy Roman Empire soldiers stared down a French company of equal size in the middle of a valley. The level of detail in this encounter was pretty impressive, as each individual soldier could be inspected, and their equipment and power level evaluated.

My favorite texture here was how troops were divided into three types: Household, Mercenary, and Levies – particularly how that difference impacted their effectiveness in battle. Household troops, who come from noble backgrounds and are the best equipped, are naturally also the most costly and difficult to train, but pay off by being highly effective in combat. Meanwhile, Mercenary troops are hired professional fighters with middling potential, while Levies, conscripted soldiers fighting because they were forced to, are down at the bottom. The main stat that determines the effectiveness of these groups is “cohesion,” which determines how well these troops work together. For example, the high-cohesion Household troops were tightly and efficiently packed together in formation and able to withstand stampeding cavalry fairly well, if properly armed for the job, while Levies were spread far apart, tended to be broken apart easily by charging enemies, and were even sometimes armed with farming equipment like pitchforks instead of real weapons of war. Seeing these disparate groups interact with one another in battle was quite fascinating to watch!

The strategy part of Chronicles: Medieval is pretty similar to something you might expect from a proper strategy/sandbox game, where you’re floating above the area and issuing commands to each part of your army individually. For example, you might want to send your cavalry ahead and flank around behind the enemy, while you send infantry forward and tell them to enter special formations like the “spearwall” that’s highly effective against mounted units. During this battle planning phase, you can augment all sorts of things with your armies as you chart out a winning strategy, like how you can thin out your men across a wider area, which gives them better coverage, but makes them more susceptible to charging enemies by spreading themselves too thin. It’s also a neat touch that, once the battle starts and the arrows start flying, you can issue additional, real-time commands, and only those units who haven’t received more specific instructions from you earlier will comply.

They also showed us the commander taking the field themselves, which transitioned things from an eye-in-the-sky view to a third-person perspective, complete with action-packed melee combat. Either on a mount, where crossing the battlefield and taking down enemies from a relatively safe distance also made it easier to bark updated orders to your men, or on foot, where it was much easier to impose your will on specific enemies that were giving your troops trouble, both of which looked like a blast.

Unfortunately, before I got to see too much of this, we did encounter a crash that abruptly shut down the demo, which is why it’s probably a good time to highlight the early access nature of this ambitious strategy game. As the first project from Raw Power Games, which is by their own account in a quite unfinished state, it will likely be a while before this lofty beast of a project doesn't have some serious rough patches. If you’re at all averse to the sometimes rocky process of playing a game before it hits 1.0, this one might be especially tough to stomach with how much it’s swinging for the fences. But if it gets there, buckle up.
While you're here, check out these previews of other big upcoming games we've played recently!
Travis Northup is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on Twitter @TieGuyTravis and read his games coverage here .
